ei.title: The Paradox of Wealth and Stress
ei.subject: 올림포스전국연합고1_2026

fullPassage: Few people will be surprised to hear that poverty tends to create stress: a 2006 study published in the American journal Psychosomatic Medicine, for example, noted that a lower socioeconomic status was associated with higher levels of stress hormones in the body. However, richer economies have their own distinct stresses. The key issue is time pressure. A 1999 study of 31 countries by American psychologist Robert Levine and Canadian psychologist Ara Norenzayan found that wealthier, more industrialized nations had a faster pace of life — which led to a higher standard of living, but at the same time left the population feeling a constant sense of urgency, as well as being more prone to heart disease. In effect, fast-paced productivity creates wealth, but it also leads people to feel time-poor when they lack the time to relax and enjoy themselves.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ noting → noted: 주절의 본동사로 과거형 noted가 필요
det.analysis:
✅ ① surprised: 'be surprised to hear'에서 감정 형용사 — 적절
✅ ② published: 과거분사의 후치수식 — 적절
❌ ③ noting → noted: 'a 2006 study noted that'에서 과거형 본동사 필요 ←정답
✅ ④ associated: 수동태 'was associated with' — 적절
det.tip: 주절에는 시제 있는 본동사(noted) 필수

questions.passage: Few people will be surprised to hear that poverty ①<u>tends</u> to create stress: a 2006 study published in the American journal Psychosomatic Medicine, for example, noted that a lower socioeconomic status was associated with higher levels of stress hormones in the body. In effect, fast-paced productivity creates wealth, but it also leads people to feel time-poor when they lack the time to relax and enjoy themselves.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ felt → feeling: leave + O + V-ing 구문에서 현재분사 feeling이 적절
det.analysis:
✅ ① tends: 주어 poverty(3인칭 단수)의 동사 — 적절
✅ ② wealthier: 비교급 형용사 — 적절
✅ ③ faster: 비교급 형용사 — 적절
❌ ④ felt → feeling: 'left the population feeling'에서 leave + O + V-ing 구문. felt(과거분사)는 부적절 ←정답
det.tip: leave + O + V-ing: left the population feeling (O가 ~하는 상태로 두다)

questions.passage: Few people will be surprised to hear that poverty tends to create stress: a 2006 study published in the American journal Psychosomatic Medicine, for example, noted that a lower socioeconomic status was associated with higher levels of stress hormones in the body. However, richer economies have their own distinct stresses. The key issue is time pressure. A 1999 study of 31 countries by American psychologist Robert Levine and Canadian psychologist Ara Norenzayan found that wealthier, more industrialized nations had a faster pace of life — ①<u>what</u> led to a higher standard of living, but at the same time ②<u>left</u> the population feeling a constant sense of urgency, as well as ③<u>being</u> more prone to heart disease. In effect, fast-paced productivity creates wealth, but it also leads people to feel time-poor when they lack the time ④<u>to relax</u> and enjoy themselves.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① what → which: 계속적 용법의 관계대명사 which가 필요. what은 선행사 포함이라 불가
det.analysis:
❌ ① what → which: '— which led to a higher standard'에서 앞 절 전체를 받는 계속적 용법 which. what은 선행사 포함이므로 불가 ←정답

✅ ② left: leave + O + C 과거형 — 적절

✅ ③ being: 'as well as being more prone'에서 as well as + V-ing — 적절

✅ ④ to relax: 'lack the time to relax'에서 to부정사의 형용사적 용법 — 적절
det.tip: which(계속적 용법): 앞 절 전체를 선행사로 받음. what = the thing which (선행사 포함)

questions.passage: Few people will be surprised to hear that poverty tends to create stress: a 2006 study published in the American journal Psychosomatic Medicine, for example, noted that a lower socioeconomic status was associated with higher levels of stress hormones in the body. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ② poorer(더 가난한) → wealthier(더 부유한): 더 부유한 산업화된 국가들이 더 빠른 생활 속도를 가졌다는 맥락
det.analysis:
✅ ① distinct: 고유한 스트레스 — 적절

❌ ② poorer → wealthier: 원문 'wealthier, more industrialized nations'. poorer로 바꾸면 가난한 국가가 더 빠른 생활을 한다는 뜻 — 문맥 모순 ←정답

✅ ③ urgency: 끊임없는 긴박감 — 적절

✅ ④ wealth: 생산성이 부를 창출한다 — 적절
det.tip: wealthier nations ↔ poorer nations

questions.passage: Few people will be surprised to hear that poverty tends to create stress: a 2006 study published in the American journal Psychosomatic Medicine, for example, noted that a lower socioeconomic status was associated with higher levels of stress hormones in the body. det.korean: ④ prevents(방지하다) → leads(이끌다): 생산성이 사람들을 시간 빈곤으로 '이끈다'는 맥락에서 '방지하다'는 반대 의미

✅ ① richer: 더 부유한 경제 — 적절

✅ ② faster: 더 빠른 생활 속도 — 적절

✅ ③ constant: 끊임없는 긴박감 — 적절

❌ ④ prevents → leads: 원문 'leads people to feel time-poor'. prevents로 바꾸면 정반대 ←정답
det.tip: leads people to feel = 사람들이 느끼게 만든다

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸: 사람들에게 끊임없는 긴박감을 느끼게 만들었다
det.analysis:
❌ ① left satisfied: 만족시켰다는 의미는 부정적 맥락(but at the same time)과 불일치

❌ ② reduction in stress: 스트레스 감소는 문맥과 반대

❌ ④ enjoy leisure time: 여가 시간 증가는 시간 압박 문맥과 모순
det.tip: but at the same time → 부정적 결과가 와야 함

ch: left the population satisfied with their pace

questions.passage: Few people will be surprised to hear that poverty tends to create stress: a 2006 study published in the American journal Psychosomatic Medicine, for example, noted that a lower socioeconomic status was associated with higher levels of stress hormones in the body. However, richer economies have <u>their own distinct stresses</u>. The key issue is time pressure. A 1999 study of 31 countries by American psychologist Robert Levine and Canadian psychologist Ara Norenzayan found that wealthier, more industrialized nations had a faster pace of life — which led to a higher standard of living, but at the same time left the population feeling a constant sense of urgency, as well as being more prone to heart disease. In effect, fast-paced productivity creates wealth, but it also leads people to feel time-poor when they lack the time to relax and enjoy themselves.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 their own distinct stresses에서 their가 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ③ 'richer economies have their own distinct stresses'에서 their는 richer economies를 가리킴
det.analysis:
❌ ① 빈곤층 사람들: their의 선행사는 poverty가 아닌 richer economies

❌ ② 연구자들: 연구자가 스트레스를 '가진다'는 문맥이 아님

✅ ③ 부유한 경제들: 'richer economies have their(= richer economies') own distinct stresses' ←정답

❌ ④ 노동자들: 개인이 아닌 경제 전체를 가리킴
det.tip: their = richer economies. 부유한 경제가 '그들의' 고유한 스트레스를 가진다
